concepts.title: Jahnavi's Dream of Going to School
concepts.section: The Day the River Spoke, Let us read
concepts.definition: Jahnavi, nearly ten and always told 'maybe later', dreams of learning to read like her brothers; with the River's push she slips into a classroom, and the teacher's visit opens the school's door for her.
concepts.key_idea: The story stands for every girl kept from school: one brave step, backed by support, ends the waiting.

concepts.title: The River as Friend and Guide
concepts.section: The Day the River Spoke, Let us read
concepts.definition: The River is written as a kind, knowing companion who listens to Jahnavi's sorrows, answers her whys, and nudges her to act for herself, reminding her that it is up to her.
concepts.key_idea: A friend guide does not solve the problem but gives courage and a plan, as the River does for Jahnavi.

concepts.title: Overcoming Fear: Jahnavi's First Step
concepts.section: The Day the River Spoke, Let us think and reflect
concepts.definition: Jahnavi fears being chased out of school, yet she walks in, sits at the back and listens; the repeated words 'I couldn't' give way to 'I did it', showing fear beaten by action.
concepts.key_idea: Courage is not the absence of fear but doing the feared thing despite a dry throat, as Jahnavi shows.

solution_steps.explain: State exactly what Jahnavi is afraid will happen to her.

Compare her words before and after to show the fear was beaten.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Slithered, Murmuring and Thicket
concepts.section: The Day the River Spoke, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Nature words carry the setting: slithered means moved by sliding from side to side, murmuring means speaking in a low voice, a thicket is a dense group of bushes and trees, and wailed means complained loudly.
concepts.key_idea: Sensory verbs like slithered and shrieked place the reader beside the river with Jahnavi.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the River tell Jahnavi that little girls can do as much as little boys?

solution_template.explain: Jahnavi believes she is too old and too scared to be allowed in school.
The River points out that girls swim as fast as boys, so nothing but habit keeps them back.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How did the teacher respond when she found Jahnavi in the class?

solution_template.explain: Jahnavi creeps in and sits quietly at the back with little Appu asleep on her shoulder.
Instead of turning her out, the teacher says she will speak to Jahnavi's father and find a way.
